question: did a recent feature flag change cause errors for customers?

systems.stop_reason: frontier exhausted (no more leads to follow)

answers.flat-RAG:
Yes. According to **INC1170**, shortly after a feature flag was disabled in feature-flag-service, a subset of users began receiving HTTP 500 errors on checkout.

Root cause: feature-flag-service's client cache served a **stale cached copy** of the flag value to some instances even after the flag was turned off, so those instances kept executing a code path that assumed the flag was still enabled.

Resolution: On-call manually flushed the feature-flag-service client cache cluster-wide, which resolved the errors within minutes.

Note from the ticket: this was **not the first occurrence** of this pattern — there is currently no automatic cache invalidation when a flag value changes, only a TTL-based expiry, so similar incidents could recur after future flag changes.

answers.ESG (v2):
## Direct Answer

**Yes.** A feature flag change did cause customer-facing errors. Per incident **INC1170**, shortly after a feature flag was disabled in `feature-flag-service`, a subset of users began receiving HTTP 500 errors on **checkout**. The root cause was not the flag change itself but a **stale cached copy of the flag value** served by the client cache — some instances kept executing the old code path (assuming the flag was still enabled) after it had been turned off.

## Supporting Evidence

- **INC1170** (servicenow, status: Resolved): Documents the incident directly — a flag was disabled in `feature-flag-service`, and a stale cached flag value caused a subset of users to hit 500 errors on checkout. The resolution notes explicitly state on-call had to manually flush the feature-flag-service client cache cluster-wide to resolve it, and that "this is not the first time" this class of issue has occurred, since there was no automatic invalidation — only a cache TTL.

- **PR-555** (gitrepo, status: Merged): A follow-up hardening change to `feature-flag-service`, adding an explicit cache-invalidation hook so flag changes propagate immediately instead of relying solely on the TTL. The PR description corroborates the incident's finding — that stale cached flag values have caused unexpected behavior after flag changes, previously requiring manual cluster-wide cache flushes. Reviewer **Fatima Al-Sayed** approved with the comment "Good catch that TTL alone wasn't enough here." Notably, this PR was **not formally linked to INC1170** in the ticketing system — it was opened directly as a proactive fix after the gap was noticed.

## Summary

The graph confirms the causal chain: feature flag disabled → stale cache served old flag state → checkout errors (INC1170) → fix merged in PR-555 to add explicit cache invalidation. The graph does not show a formal ticket-to-PR link (e.g., PR-555 "fixes" INC1170), so while the two are clearly related in substance, that linkage is inferred from matching descriptions rather than an explicit tracked reference.
